[{"content": "MERIDIAN ADVANCED MANUFACTURING INC.
Precision Engineering  |  Aerospace  |  Automotive  |  Industrial Equipment
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
1.  BACKGROUND
Meridian Advanced Manufacturing Inc. is a mid-market precision manufacturing company operating four production facilities across the United States. Since our founding, we have built a reputation for delivering high-tolerance, precision-engineered components to clients in the aerospace, automotive, and industrial equipment sectors. Our total revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $187 million, supported by a workforce of approximately 820 employees across all plants.
Our manufacturing footprint is as follows:
The Columbus plant is our oldest and largest facility, serving as the primary production hub for our aerospace clients. Portland and Nashville were established to expand capacity and diversify our manufacturing capabilities into adjacent markets. The Phoenix plant represents our strategic investment in next-generation manufacturing technologies, including additive manufacturing and advanced composite materials.
2.  CURRENT SITUATION
The Board of Directors has expressed significant concern regarding several converging operational challenges that are eroding our competitive position and financial performance. I am requesting this assessment because the data from the first half of 2024 suggests these issues are systemic and require a structured, analytically rigorous response.
The primary areas of concern are:
Declining Operating Margins: Our consolidated operating margin declined from 14.2% in FY2022 to 11.8% in FY2023, representing a 240-basis-point compression. Preliminary Q1/Q2 2024 figures suggest this trend is continuing, with operating margin tracking at approximately 10.9%. If unaddressed, this trajectory will jeopardize our ability to fund planned capital investments and maintain competitive pricing.
Quality Escalations: Several of our key accounts—including two Tier 1 aerospace OEMs—have formally escalated quality complaints over the past two quarters. Our internal quality metrics show an increase in defect rates, particularly at the Columbus and Portland plants. Customer satisfaction scores have declined from 4.3/5.0 in FY2022 to 3.7/5.0 in the most recent survey period.
Portland Delivery Performance: The Portland plant has experienced a marked decline in on-time delivery performance over the past two quarters, falling from 94.1% in Q3/Q4 2023 to an estimated 87.3% in Q1/Q2 2024. This is below our contractual SLA threshold of 92% for several accounts and poses a material risk to client retention.
Columbus Equipment & Maintenance: The Columbus facility, our oldest plant, is experiencing escalating unplanned maintenance events. Equipment downtime has increased roughly 18% year-over-year, and maintenance expenditures now represent a disproportionate share of the plant's operating costs. Several critical CNC machines are approaching end-of-life and require either major overhaul or replacement.
Phoenix Ramp-Up Delays: Despite being operational for over two years, the Phoenix facility has not yet achieved its targeted capacity utilization rate of 72%. Current utilization is estimated at approximately 58%, resulting in higher-than-projected per-unit costs and an extended timeline to achieve return on the initial capital investment.
3.  SCOPE OF WORK
I am engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive operational efficiency assessment covering the first two quarters of fiscal year 2024. The assessment should be data-driven, benchmarked against recognized industry standards, and grounded in established operational excellence methodologies. Specifically, I am asking the management analyst team to undertake the following:
Operational Data Analysis: Analyze the attached Q1/Q2 2024 operational data across all four manufacturing plants. This includes production volumes, capacity utilization, defect rates, on-time delivery metrics, labor productivity, equipment downtime, and cost breakdowns. Identify statistically significant trends, anomalies, and cross-plant performance disparities.
Industry Benchmarking: Benchmark Meridian's operational performance against relevant industry standards. Utilize the provided FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) manufacturing capacity utilization data and the manufacturing defect benchmarking dataset to contextualize our performance within the broader U.S. manufacturing sector. Identify areas where we are significantly above or below industry norms.
Bottleneck Identification: Identify the top 3–5 operational bottlenecks or systemic problem areas across the organization. For each identified issue, provide supporting data, assess the financial impact, and determine whether the root cause is related to equipment, process, workforce, or management factors.
Lean Manufacturing Best Practices: Reference established lean manufacturing principles and the EPA lean manufacturing case studies provided for reference. Assess the applicability of specific lean tools and methodologies (e.g., value stream mapping, 5S, TPM, kaizen) to Meridian's identified problem areas. Provide actionable recommendations grounded in proven industry practices.
Excel Workbook — Data Analysis & Findings: Organize all analytical findings, data summaries, benchmarking comparisons, and supporting calculations into a structured Excel workbook. The workbook should be clearly organized with separate worksheets for each major analysis area, include data visualizations where appropriate, and serve as the analytical foundation for the executive presentation.
Executive PowerPoint Presentation: Prepare a professional PowerPoint presentation of approximately 15–20 slides for the executive leadership team. The presentation should cover: (a) current state assessment with key performance metrics, (b) industry benchmarking analysis, (c) identified operational problems with root cause analysis, (d) prioritized recommendations with estimated financial impact and implementation timeline, and (e) a proposed roadmap for operational improvement initiatives.
4.  KEY QUESTIONS TO ADDRESS
The following questions should serve as a guiding framework for the analysis. The executive committee will expect clear, evidence-based answers to each of these in the final presentation:
Which plant(s) require the most urgent operational intervention, and what specific evidence supports this prioritization?
What are the primary drivers of the declining consolidated operating margin? To what extent are these driven by cost inflation, operational inefficiency, pricing pressure, or product mix changes?
How does Meridian's capacity utilization across each plant compare to the national manufacturing average as reported by the Federal Reserve? Where are the largest gaps?

[{"content": "All analyses are complete. Now I'll build the three deliverables with a single comprehensive script.<tool_call>write<arg_key>content</arg_key><arg_value>#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build Meridian deliverables: Excel diagnostic workbook, COPQ CSV, strategic memo DOCX."""
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
from openpyxl.chart import BarChart, Reference
import docx
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT

SRC = '/work/task_folder'
OUT = '/work/output'
order = ['Jan-2024','Feb-2024','Mar-2024','Apr-2024','May-2024','Jun-2024']
SEV_W = {'Critical':5000,'High':2500,'Medium':1000,'Low':250}
SEV_N = {'Critical':4,'High':3,'Medium':2,'Low':1}

prod = pd.read_excel(f'{SRC}/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Monthly_Production_Data')
emp  = pd.read_excel(f'{SRC}/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Employee_Headcount')
eq   = pd.read_excel(f'{SRC}/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Equipment_Inventory')
comp = pd.read_csv(f'{SRC}/Meridian_Customer_Complaints_Q1Q2_2024.csv')
bench= pd.read_csv(f'{SRC}/manufacturing_defect_dataset.csv')
fred = pd.read_csv(f'{SRC}/references/FRED_manufacturing_capacity_utilization.csv',parse_dates=['observation_date'])
fred6 = fred[(fred.observation_date>='2024-01-01')&(fred.observation_date<='2024-06-01')].reset_index(drop=True)
FRED_AVG = fred6.MCUMFN.mean()

plants = ['Columbus OH','Nashville TN','Phoenix AZ','Portland OR']

# ================= AGGREGATES =================
g = prod.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(
    units=('Production_Volume_Units','sum'), target=('Production_Target_Units','sum'),
    act_h=('Actual_Output_Hours','sum'), plan_h=('Planned_Output_Hours','sum'),
    defects=('Defect_Count','sum'), rework=('Units_Reworked','sum'), scrap=('Scrap_Units','sum'),
    mat=('Raw_Material_Cost_USD','sum'), labor=('Labor_Cost_USD','sum'),
    maint=('Maintenance_Cost_USD','sum'), dt_unp=('Downtime_Hours_Unplanned','sum'),
    dt_plan=('Downtime_Hours_Planned','sum'), returns=('Customer_Returns','sum')).reindex(plants)
g['otd'] = prod.groupby('Plant_Name').apply(
    lambda d: np.average(d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct, weights=d.Production_Volume_Units), include_groups=False).reindex(plants)
g['avail'] = g.act_h/g.plan_h
g['perf']  = g.units/g.target
g['qual']  = 1-g.defects/g.units
g['OEE']   = g.avail*g.perf*g.qual
g['def1000'] = g.defects/g.units*1000
g['dtpct'] = g.dt_unp/g.plan_h*100
g['cost_unit'] = (g.mat+g.labor+g.maint)/g.units
g['util'] = g.units/g.target*100
g['maint_share'] = g.maint/(g.mat+g.labor+g.maint)*100

# composite score (min-max normalized, equal weights; higher=better)
def norm(s, invert=False):
    r = (s-s.min())/(s.max()-s.min())
    return 1-r if invert else r
comp_score = (norm(g.OEE)*0.2 + norm(g.def1000,True)*0.2 + norm(g.otd)*0.2 +
              norm(g.dtpct,True)*0.2 + norm(g.cost_unit,True)*0.2)*100
g['composite'] = comp_score
g['rank'] = g['composite'].rank(ascending=False).astype(int)

# plant-month aggregates
pm = prod.copy(); pm['mi'] = pm.Month.map({m:i for i,m in enumerate(order)})
pma = pm.groupby(['Plant_Name','Month']).apply(lambda d: pd.Series({
    'units':d.Production_Volume_Units.sum(),'target':d.Production_Target_Units.sum(),
    'def1000':d.Defect_Count.sum()/d.Production_Volume_Units.sum()*1000,
    'otd':np.average(d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct,weights=d.Production_Volume_Units),
    'dt_unp':d.Downtime_Hours_Unplanned.sum()}), include_groups=False).reset_index()
pma['mi']=pma.Month.map({m:i for i,m in enumerate(order)}); pma=pma.sort_values(['Plant_Name','mi'])

plant_slopes = {}
for p,d in pma.groupby('Plant_Name'):
    plant_slopes[p] = (np.polyfit(d.mi,d.def1000,1)[0], np.polyfit(d.mi,d.otd,1)[0])

# combo watch items
pc = prod.copy(); pc['def1000']=pc.Defect_Count/pc.Production_Volume_Units*1000
pc['attain']=pc.Production_Volume_Units/pc.Production_Target_Units*100
pc['mi']=pc.Month.map({m:i for i,m in enumerate(order)})
combo_rows=[]
for (p,pl),d in pc.groupby(['Plant_Name','Product_Line']):
    d=d.sort_values('mi')
    def_adv=int((np.diff(d.def1000.values)>0).sum())
    otd_adv=int((np.diff(d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct.values)<0).sum())
    att_adv=int((np.diff(d.attain.values)<0).sum())
    sl=lambda c: np.polyfit(d.mi,d[c],1)[0]
    fl=[def_adv>=3,otd_adv>=3,att_adv>=3]
    combo_rows.append(dict(Plant=p,Line=pl,
        def_jan=d.def1000.iloc[0],def_jun=d.def1000.iloc[-1],def_slope=sl('def1000'),def_adv=def_adv,
        otd_jan=d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct.iloc[0],otd_jun=d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct.iloc[-1],otd_slope=sl('On_Time_Delivery_Pct'),otd_adv=otd_adv,
        att_jan=d.attain.iloc[0],att_jun=d.attain.iloc[-1],att_slope=sl('attain'),att_adv=att_adv,
        nflags=sum(fl),watch=int(sum(fl)>=2)))
combos=pd.DataFrame(combo_rows).sort_values(['watch','Plant','Line'],ascending=[False,True,True])

# ================= COPQ =================
gg = g.copy()
gg['mat_unit']=gg.mat/gg.units; gg['lab_unit']=gg.labor/gg.units; gg['hr_rate']=gg.labor/gg.act_h
cs = comp.groupby(['Plant_Name','Severity']).size().unstack(fill_value=0).reindex(index=plants,columns=['Critical','High','Medium','Low'],fill_value=0)
gg['scrap_c']=gg.scrap*gg.mat_unit
gg['rework_c']=gg.rework*0.4*gg.lab_unit
gg['ret_c']=gg.returns*gg.mat_unit
gg['compl_c']=sum(cs[s]*SEV_W[s] for s in SEV_W)
gg['dt_c']=gg.dt_unp*gg.hr_rate
gg['total_copq']=gg[['scrap_c','rework_c','ret_c','compl_c','dt_c']].sum(axis=1)
gg['prod_cost']=gg.mat+gg.labor+gg.maint
gg['copq_pct']=gg.total_copq/gg.prod_cost*100
tot = gg[['scrap','rework','returns','scrap_c','rework_c','ret_c','compl_c','dt_c','total_copq','prod_cost','mat','labor','maint','dt_unp','act_h','labor']].sum()
tot_units=g.units.sum(); tot_mat_unit=tot.mat/tot_units; tot_lab_unit=tot.labor/tot_units
tot_rate=tot.labor/tot.act_h
tot_sev=comp.Severity.value_counts()
summary = {
 'scrap_c':tot.scrap*tot_mat_unit,'rework_c':tot.rework*0.4*tot_lab_unit,'ret_c':tot.returns*tot_mat_unit,
 'compl_c':sum(tot_sev.get(s,0)*SEV_W[s] for s in SEV_W),'dt_c':tot.dt_unp*tot_rate}
summary['total_copq']=sum(summary.values()); summary['prod_cost']=tot.prod_cost
summary['copq_pct']=summary['total_copq']/summary['prod_cost']*100

# ================= COMPLAINT CROSSREF =================
comp['mkey']=pd.to_datetime(comp.Date_Received).dt.month
comp['sev']=comp.Severity.map(SEV_N)
pm2=prod.copy(); pm2['mkey']=pd.to_datetime(pm2.Month,format='%b-%Y').dt.month
j=comp.groupby(['Plant_Name','mkey']).agg(Complaints=('Complaint_ID','count'),Avg_Severity=('sev','mean'),
    Severity_Load=('sev','sum')).reset_index()
jj=pm2.groupby(['Plant_Name','mkey']).agg(Units=('Production_Volume_Units','sum'),
    Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs=('Downtime_Hours_Unplanned','sum')).reset_index()
xref=j.merge(jj,on=['Plant_Name','mkey'],how='right').fillna({'Complaints':0,'Avg_Severity':0,'Severity_Load':0})
xref['Month']=xref.mkey.map({i:m for m,i in enumerate(order,1)})
xref['Complaint_Rate_per_1000']=xref.Complaints/xref.Units*1000
xref=xref.sort_values(['Plant_Name','mkey'])
mc=xref[xref.Complaints>0]
def spear(x,y): return np.corrcoef(x.rank(),y.rank())[0,1]
corr_all_n   = (xref.Complaints.corr(xref.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs), spear(xref.Complaints,xref.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs))
corr_sev_dt  = (mc.Avg_Severity.corr(mc.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs), spear(mc.Avg_Severity,mc.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs))
corr_load_dt = (xref.Severity_Load.corr(xref.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs), spear(xref.Severity_Load,xref.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs))
plant_xref = xref.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(Complaints=('Complaints','sum'),Units=('Units','sum'),
    Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs=('Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs','sum'),Avg_Sev_When=('Avg_Severity',lambda s: s[s>0].mean()))
plant_xref['Rate_per_1000']=plant_xref.Complaints/plant_xref.Units*1000
per_plant_corr={}
for p,d in xref.groupby('Plant_Name'):
    dd=d[d.Complaints>0]
    per_plant_corr[p]=(d.Complaints.corr(d.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs), dd.Avg_Severity.corr(dd.Unplanned_Downtime_Hrs))
cat_by_plant = comp.pivot_table(index='Plant_Name',columns='Complaint_Category',values='Complaint_ID',aggfunc='count',fill_value=0)

# ================= EQUIPMENT =================
eq['Age_Years']=2024-eq.Year_Installed
eq['Yrs_Since_Overhaul']=2024-pd.to_datetime(eq.Last_Major_Overhaul,format='%b-%Y').dt.year
eq['Priority']=np.where((eq.Age_Years>8)&(eq.Condition_Rating_1to10<=5),'REPLACE',
                np.where(eq.Age_Years>8,'MONITOR','OK'))
eq_x=eq.merge(g[['dtpct','def1000']].rename(columns={'dtpct':'Plant_Downtime_Pct','def1000':'Plant_Def_per_1000'}),on='Plant_Name')
eq_roll=eq.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(Items=('Equipment_ID','count'),Avg_Age=('Age_Years','mean'),
    Avg_Condition=('Condition_Rating_1to10','mean'),Avg_Mo_Downtime=('Avg_Monthly_Downtime_Hours','mean'),
    Replace_Items=('Priority',lambda s:(s=='REPLACE').sum()),Capital=('Replacement_Cost_USD',lambda s: s[eq.loc[s.index,'Priority']=='REPLACE'].sum())).reindex(plants)

# ================= EMPLOYEES =================
eh=emp.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(FT=('Headcount_FT','sum'),PT=('Headcount_PT','sum'),
    Tenure=('Avg_Tenure_Years','mean'),Turnover=('Turnover_Rate_Pct_Annual','mean'),
    Training=('Avg_Training_Hours_Per_Employee','mean')).reindex(plants)
eh['Total']=eh.FT+eh.PT
eh['Units_per_Emp']=g.units/eh.Total

# ================= VERIFICATION PRINTS =================
print("=== SCORECARD ==="); print(g[['OEE','avail','perf','qual','def1000','otd','dtpct','cost_unit','util','composite','rank','maint_share']].round(3).to_string())
print("=== PLANT SLOPES ==="); print({k:(round(v[0],3),round(v[1],3)) for k,v in plant_slopes.items()})
print("=== WATCH ==="); print(combos[combos.watch==1][['Plant','Line']].values.tolist())
print("=== FRED avg ===", round(FRED_AVG,2), fred6.MCUMFN.round(2).tolist())
print("=== PORTLAND OTD monthly ===", prod[prod.Plant_Name=='Portland OR'].groupby('Month').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct,weights=d.Production_Volume_Units),include_groups=False).reindex(order).round(1).to_dict())
print("=== COPQ pct ===", gg.copq_pct.round(2).to_dict(), "TOTAL", round(summary['copq_pct'],2), round(summary['total_copq'],0))
print("=== corr ===", [round(c,3) for c in (corr_all_n[0],corr_all_n[1],corr_sev_dt[0],corr_sev_dt[1],corr_load_dt[0],corr_load_dt[1])])
print("=== per plant corr ===", {k:(round(v[0],2),round(v[1],2)) for k,v in per_plant_corr.items()})
print("=== complaint rate ===", plant_xref.Rate_per_1000.round(2).to_dict())
print("=== cats ==="); print(cat_by_plant.to_string())
print("===Portland late complaints===", comp[(comp.Plant_Name=='Portland OR')].Complaint_Category.value_counts().to_dict())
print("=== maint share ===", g.maint_share.round(1).to_dict())
print("=== equip capex ===", eq_roll.Capital.to_dict(), "total", eq[eq.Priority=='REPLACE'].Replacement_Cost_USD.sum())
print("=== turnover ===", eh.Turnover.round(1).to_dict(), "tenure", eh.Tenure.round(1).to_dict())

# ======================================================================
# DELIVERABLE 1: EXCEL WORKBOOK
# ======================================================================
wb = Workbook()
HDR_FILL = PatternFill('solid', fgColor='1F3864')
HDR_FONT = Font(color='FFFFFF', bold=True, size=10)
SUB_FILL = PatternFill('solid', fgColor='D9E2F3')
WARN_FILL= PatternFill('solid', fgColor='FCE4D6')
GOOD_FILL= PatternFill('solid', fgColor='E2EFDA')
NOTE_FONT= Font(italic=True, size=8, color='595959')
THIN = Border(*[Side(style='thin', color='BFBFBF')]*4)

def style_header(ws, row, ncols, start_col=1):
    for c in range(start_col, start_col+ncols):
        cell = ws.cell(row=row, column=c)
        cell.fill=HDR_FILL; cell.font=HDR_FONT
        cell.alignment=Alignment(horizontal='center', vertical='center', wrap_text=True)
        cell.border=THIN

def put(ws, r, c, v, fmt=None, bold=False, fill=None, align=None):
    cell=ws.cell(row=r, column=c, value=v)
    if fmt: cell.number_format=fmt
    if bold: cell.font=Font(bold=True)
    if fill: cell.fill=PatternFill('solid', fgColor=fill)
    if align: cell.alignment=Alignment(horizontal=align)
    cell.border=THIN
    return cell

def title(ws, r, text, sub=None):
    ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=text).font=Font(bold=True, size=13, color='1F3864')
    if sub:
        ws.cell(row=r+1, column=1, value=sub).font=NOTE_FONT
        return r+2
    return r+1

# ---- Tab 1: Plant Scorecard ----
ws = wb.active; ws.title='Plant Scorecard'
r = title(ws,1,'MERIDIAN ADVANCED MANUFACTURING — PLANT SCORECARD (Q1–Q2 2024, Jan–Jun aggregate)',
    'Metrics computed from Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx (Monthly_Production_Data, 72 plant-month-line records). Composite = equal-weighted min-max normalized score (0–100) across the five metrics below; higher = healthier.')
r+=1
cols=['Plant','OEE','Availability','Performance','Quality','Defects per 1,000 Units','Avg On-Time Delivery %','Unplanned Downtime % of Planned Hours','Cost per Unit ($)','Composite Score (0–100)','Rank']
for i,c in enumerate(cols,1): ws.cell(row=r,column=i,value=c)
style_header(ws,r,len(cols)); hdr=r
r+=1
for p in plants:
    row=g.loc[p]
    put(ws,r,1,p,bold=True); put(ws,r,2,row.OEE,'0.0%'); put(ws,r,3,row.avail,'0.0%'); put(ws,r,4,row.perf,'0.0%')
    put(ws,r,5,row.qual,'0.0%'); put(ws,r,6,row.def1000,'0.0'); put(ws,r,7,row.otd/100,'0.0%')
    put(ws,r,8,row.dtpct/100,'0.00%'); put(ws,r,9,row.cost_unit,'$#,##0.00')
    put(ws,r,10,row.composite,'0.0'); put(ws,r,11,int(row.rank),'0',
        fill=GOOD_FILL if row.rank==1 else (WARN_FILL if row.rank==4 else None),align='center')
    if row.rank==1:
        for c in range(1,12): ws.cell(row=r,column=c).fill=PatternFill('solid',fgColor='E2EFDA')
    r+=1
r+=1
ws.cell(row=r,column=1,value='OEE = Availability (actual/planned output hours) × Performance (units vs target) × Quality (1 − defects/units).').font=NOTE_FONT
ws.cell(row=r+1,column=1,value='Cost per unit = (raw material + labor + maintenance) / units; energy is reported only in kWh (no $ rate provided) and is excluded. OTD is volume-weighted monthly average.').font=NOTE_FONT
ws.cell(row=r+2,column=1,value='Ranking: 1 = Nashville TN (healthiest) … 4 = Phoenix AZ. Composite weights are equal (20% per metric).').font=NOTE_FONT
chart=BarChart(); chart.type='col'; chart.title='OEE by Plant (H1 2024)'; chart.height=7; chart.width=13
data=Reference(ws,min_col=2,min_row=hdr,max_row=hdr+4); cats=Reference(ws,min_col=1,min_row=hdr+1,max_row=hdr+4)
chart.add_data(data,titles_from_data=True); chart.set_categories(cats); chart.y_axis.numFmt='0%'
ws.add_chart(chart,f'A{r+4}')
chart2=BarChart(); chart2.type='col'; chart2.title='Defects per 1,000 Units (H1 2024)'; chart2.height=7; chart2.width=13
data2=Reference(ws,min_col=6,min_row=hdr,max_row=hdr+4)
chart2.add_data(data2,titles_from_data=True); chart2.set_categories(cats)
ws.add_chart(chart2,f'H{r+4}')
for col,w in zip('ABCDEFGHIJK',[16,10,12,12,10,14,12,16,13,14,7]): ws.column_dimensions[col].width=w

# ---- Tab 2: Trend Diagnostics ----
ws = wb.create_sheet('Trend Diagnostics')
r = title(ws,1,'TREND DIAGNOSTICS — DETERIORATION FLAGGING (Jan–Jun 2024)',
  'A metric is flagged "deteriorating" if it worsened month-over-month in ≥3 of the 5 transitions (defect rate up / OTD down / target attainment down). Plant–product line combos failing on ≥2 metrics are WATCH ITEMS.')
r+=1
ws.cell(row=r,column=1,value='A. Plant × Product Line Watch Items').font=Font(bold=True,size=11,color='1F3864'); r+=1
cols=['Plant','Product Line','Defect/1k Jan','Defect/1k Jun','Defect Slope (/mo)','Adv MoM (Def)','OTD% Jan','OTD% Jun','OTD Slope (pp/mo)','Adv MoM (OTD)','Attainment% Jan','Attainment% Jun','Attainment Slope (pp/mo)','Adv MoM (Att)','Flags','Watch Item']
for i,c in enumerate(cols,1): ws.cell(row=r,column=i,value=c)
style_header(ws,r,len(cols)); r+=1
for _,row in combos.iterrows():
    fill = WARN_FILL if row.watch else None
    vals=[row.Plant,row.Line,row.def_jan,row.def_jun,row.def_slope,row.def_adv,row.otd_jan,row.otd_jun,
          row.otd_slope,row.otd_adv,row.att_jan,row.att_jun,row.att_slope,row.att_adv,row.nflags,'WATCH' if row.watch else '']
    for i,v in enumerate(vals,1):
        fmt='0.00' if isinstance(v,float) else ('0' if isinstance(v,(int,np.integer)) else None)
        put(ws,r,i,v,fmt,fill=fill,align='center' if i in (6,10,14,15,16) else None)
    r+=1
r+=1
ws.cell(row=r,column=1,value='B. Plant-Level 6-Month Trend Slopes (aggregate across product lines)').font=Font(bold=True,size=11,color='1F3864'); r+=1
cols=['Plant','Aggregate Defect Rate Slope (per 1,000 units per month)','Aggregate OTD Slope (percentage points per month)','Interpretation']
for i,c in enumerate(cols,1): ws.cell(row=r,column=i,value=c)
style_header(ws,r,len(cols)); r+=1
for p in plants:
    sd,so=plant_slopes[p]
    interp=[]
    interp.append('defects rising' if sd>0.3 else ('defects improving' if sd<-0.3 else 'defects stable'))
    interp.append('OTD deteriorating' if so<-0.3 else ('OTD improving' if so>0.3 else 'OTD stable'))
    put(ws,r,1,p,bold=True); put(ws,r,2,sd,'+0.000;-0.000'); put(ws,r,3,so,'+0.000;-0.000')
    put(ws,r,4,'; '.join(interp))

COPQ varies 3.2× between best and worst plant with an identical footprint; equalizing COPQ ratios recovers ~$0.5M annualized without any capital restructuring. Third, equipment: the replacement need is concentrated at Columbus ($2.66M, 5 of 28 assets) — a targeted capital fix, not a network redesign. Fourth, workforce: Phoenix\'s 23.2% turnover and 2.4-year tenure (vs 9.8%/12.5 years at Columbus) indicate ramp-up stabilization is achievable in place; Portland\'s logistics-driven late deliveries (its largest complaint category) do not require closing capacity. Precision Engineering  |  Aerospace  |  Automotive  |  Industrial Equipment
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
1.  BACKGROUND
Meridian Advanced Manufacturing Inc. is a mid-market precision manufacturing company operating four production facilities across the United States. Since our founding, we have built a reputation for delivering high-tolerance, precision-engineered components to clients in the aerospace, automotive, and industrial equipment sectors. Our total revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $187 million, supported by a workforce of approximately 820 employees across all plants.
Our manufacturing footprint is as follows:
The Columbus plant is our oldest and largest facility, serving as the primary production hub for our aerospace clients. Portland and Nashville were established to expand capacity and diversify our manufacturing capabilities into adjacent markets. The Phoenix plant represents our strategic investment in next-generation manufacturing technologies, including additive manufacturing and advanced composite materials.
2.  CURRENT SITUATION
The Board of Directors has expressed significant concern regarding several converging operational challenges that are eroding our competitive position and financial performance. I am requesting this assessment because the data from the first half of 2024 suggests these issues are systemic and require a structured, analytically rigorous response.
The primary areas of concern are:
Declining Operating Margins: Our consolidated operating margin declined from 14.2% in FY2022 to 11.8% in FY2023, representing a 240-basis-point compression. Preliminary Q1/Q2 2024 figures suggest this trend is continuing, with operating margin tracking at approximately 10.9%. If unaddressed, this trajectory will jeopardize our ability to fund planned capital investments and maintain competitive pricing.
Quality Escalations: Several of our key accounts—including two Tier 1 aerospace OEMs—have formally escalated quality complaints over the past two quarters. Our internal quality metrics show an increase in defect rates, particularly at the Columbus and Portland plants. Customer satisfaction scores have declined from 4.3/5.0 in FY2022 to 3.7/5.0 in the most recent survey period.
Portland Delivery Performance: The Portland plant has experienced a marked decline in on-time delivery performance over the past two quarters, falling from 94.1% in Q3/Q4 2023 to an estimated 87.3% in Q1/Q2 2024. This is below our contractual SLA threshold of 92% for several accounts and poses a material risk to client retention.
Columbus Equipment & Maintenance: The Columbus facility, our oldest plant, is experiencing escalating unplanned maintenance events. Equipment downtime has increased roughly 18% year-over-year, and maintenance expenditures now represent a disproportionate share of the plant's operating costs. Several critical CNC machines are approaching end-of-life and require either major overhaul or replacement.
Phoenix Ramp-Up Delays: Despite being operational for over two years, the Phoenix facility has not yet achieved its targeted capacity utilization rate of 72%. Current utilization is estimated at approximately 58%, resulting in higher-than-projected per-unit costs and an extended timeline to achieve return on the initial capital investment.
3.  SCOPE OF WORK
I am engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive operational efficiency assessment covering the first two quarters of fiscal year 2024. The assessment should be data-driven, benchmarked against recognized industry standards, and grounded in established operational excellence methodologies. Specifically, I am asking the management analyst team to undertake the following:
Operational Data Analysis: Analyze the attached Q1/Q2 2024 operational data across all four manufacturing plants. This includes production volumes, capacity utilization, defect rates, on-time delivery metrics, labor productivity, equipment downtime, and cost breakdowns. Identify statistically significant trends, anomalies, and cross-plant performance disparities.
Industry Benchmarking: Benchmark Meridian's operational performance against relevant industry standards. Utilize the provided FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) manufacturing capacity utilization data and the manufacturing defect benchmarking dataset to contextualize our performance within the broader U.S. manufacturing sector. Identify areas where we are significantly above or below industry norms.
Bottleneck Identification: Identify the top 3–5 operational bottlenecks or systemic problem areas across the organization. For each identified issue, provide supporting data, assess the financial impact, and determine whether the root cause is related to equipment, process, workforce, or management factors.
Lean Manufacturing Best Practices: Reference established lean manufacturing principles and the EPA lean manufacturing case studies provided for reference. Assess the applicability of specific lean tools and methodologies (e.g., value stream mapping, 5S, TPM, kaizen) to Meridian's identified problem areas. Provide actionable recommendations grounded in proven industry practices.
Excel Workbook — Data Analysis & Findings: Organize all analytical findings, data summaries, benchmarking comparisons, and supporting calculations into a structured Excel workbook. The workbook should be clearly organized with separate worksheets for each major analysis area, include data visualizations where appropriate, and serve as the analytical foundation for the executive presentation.
Executive PowerPoint Presentation: Prepare a professional PowerPoint presentation of approximately 15–20 slides for the executive leadership team. The presentation should cover: (a) current state assessment with key performance metrics, (b) industry benchmarking analysis, (c) identified operational problems with root cause analysis, (d) prioritized recommendations with estimated financial impact and implementation timeline, and (e) a proposed roadmap for operational improvement initiatives.
4.  KEY QUESTIONS TO ADDRESS
The following questions should serve as a guiding framework for the analysis. The executive committee will expect clear, evidence-based answers to each of these in the final presentation:
Which plant(s) require the most urgent operational intervention, and what specific evidence supports this prioritization?
What are the primary drivers of the declining consolidated operating margin? To what extent are these driven by cost inflation, operational inefficiency, pricing pressure, or product mix changes?
How does Meridian's capacity utilization across each plant compare to the national manufacturing average as reported by the Federal Reserve? Where are the largest gaps?
What specific lean manufacturing practices and methodologies could be adopted or expanded to measurably improve operational performance at each facility?
What is the estimated return on investment (ROI) for the top recommended improvement initiatives, including projected timeline to realization and required capital or operational investment?
5.  TIMELINE & DELIVERABLES
Given the urgency of the board's concerns, I am establishing the following timeline for this engagement:
The final presentation will be delivered to the Executive Committee on August 22, 2024. I will be present to provide operational context and support the discussion. Please plan for a 45-minute presentation followed by a 30-minute Q&A session.
6.  ATTACHMENTS & REFERENCE MATERIALS
The following data files and reference documents are provided to support your analysis. Please review all materials thoroughly before the project kickoff meeting:
■  Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx — Detailed operational data for all four plants covering January–June 2024, including monthly production volumes, capacity utilization rates, defect counts, on-time delivery rates, labor hours, equipment downtime logs, and cost allocations.
■  Meridian_Customer_Complaints_Q1Q2_2024.csv — Log of all customer complaints and quality escalations received during Q1/Q2 2024, including complaint category, severity, affected plant, product line, and resolution status.
■  FRED_manufacturing_capacity_utilization.csv — Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) time series for U.S. manufacturing sector capacity utilization, to be used as the primary benchmarking reference for capacity analysis.
■  FRED_industrial_production_manufacturing.csv — FRED industrial production index for the manufacturing sector, providing macroeconomic context for Meridian's production volume trends.
■  manufacturing_defect_dataset.csv — Industry benchmarking dataset containing defect rate data across various manufacturing sub-sectors, to be used for comparative quality analysis.
■  EPA_Lean_Manufacturing_Case_Studies.pdf — U.S. Environmental Protection Agency compilation of lean manufacturing case studies demonstrating proven efficiency improvement methodologies applicable to precision manufacturing operations.
This assessment is a high priority for both my office and the Board of Directors. I expect a thorough, analytically rigorous review that will provide the executive committee with clear visibility into our operational challenges and a credible path forward. Please do not hesitate to reach out to me or my Chief of Staff, Sarah Martinez (s.martinez@meridianmfg.com), if you require additional data, access to plant personnel, or clarification on any aspect of this engagement.
I look forward to your findings and recommendations.
Regards,
David Chen
Vice President of Operations
Meridian Advanced Manufacturing Inc.

"""Build Meridian deliverables: Excel diagnostic workbook, COPQ CSV, strategic memo DOCX."""

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter

from docx import Document

SRC = '/work/task_folder'
OUT = '/work/output'
order = ['Jan-2024','Feb-2024','Mar-2024','Apr-2024','May-2024','Jun-2024']
SEV_W = {'Critical':5000,'High':2500,'Medium':1000,'Low':250}
SEV_N = {'Critical':4,'High':3,'Medium':2,'Low':1}

prod = pd.read_excel(f'{SRC}/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Monthly_Production_Data')
emp  = pd.read_excel(f'{SRC}/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Employee_Headcount')

comp = pd.read_csv(f'{SRC}/Meridian_Customer_Complaints_Q1Q2_2024.csv')
bench= pd.read_csv(f'{SRC}/manufacturing_defect_dataset.csv')
fred = pd.read_csv(f'{SRC}/references/FRED_manufacturing_capacity_utilization.csv',parse_dates=['observation_date'])
fred6 = fred[(fred.observation_date>='2024-01-01')&(fred.observation_date<='2024-06-01')].reset_index(drop=True)
FRED_AVG = fred6.MCUMFN.mean()

plants = ['Columbus OH','Nashville TN','Phoenix AZ','Portland OR']

# ================= AGGREGATES =================
g = prod.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(
    units=('Production_Volume_Units','sum'), target=('Production_Target_Units','sum'),
    act_h=('Actual_Output_Hours','sum'), plan_h=('Planned_Output_Hours','sum'),
    defects=('Defect_Count','sum'), rework=('Units_Reworked','sum'), scrap=('Scrap_Units','sum'),
    mat=('Raw_Material_Cost_USD','sum'), labor=('Labor_Cost_USD','sum'),
    maint=('Maintenance_Cost_USD','sum'), dt_unp=('Downtime_Hours_Unplanned','sum'),
    dt_plan=('Downtime_Hours_Planned','sum'), returns=('Customer_Returns','sum')).reindex(plants)
g['otd'] = prod.groupby('Plant_Name').apply(
    lambda d: np.average(d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct, weights=d.Production_Volume_Units), include_groups=False).reindex(plants)
g['avail'] = g.act_h/g.plan_h
g['perf']  = g.units/g.target
g['qual']  = 1-g.defects/g.units
g['OEE']   = g.avail*g.perf*g.qual
g['def1000'] = g.defects/g.units*1000
g['dtpct'] = g.dt_unp/g.plan_h*100
g['cost_unit'] = (g.mat+g.labor+g.maint)/g.units
g['util'] = g.units/g.target*100
g['maint_share'] = g.maint/(g.mat+g.labor+g.maint)*100

# composite score (min-max normalized, equal weights; higher=better)
def norm(s, invert=False):
    r = (s-s.min())/(s.max()-s.min())
    return 1-r if invert else r
comp_score = (norm(g.OEE)*0.2 + norm(g.def1000,True)*0.2 + norm(g.otd)*0.2 +
              norm(g.dtpct,True)*0.2 + norm(g.cost_unit,True)*0.2)*100
g['composite'] = comp_score
g['rank'] = g['composite'].rank(ascending=False).astype(int)

# plant-month aggregates
pm = prod.copy(); pm['mi'] = pm.Month.map({m:i for i,m in enumerate(order)})
pma = pm.groupby(['Plant_Name','Month']).apply(lambda d: pd.Series({
    'units':d.Production_Volume_Units.sum(),'target':d.Production_Target_Units.sum(),
    'def1000':d.Defect_Count.sum()/d.Production_Volume_Units.sum()*1000,
    'otd':np.average(d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct,weights=d.Production_Volume_Units),
    'dt_unp':d.Downtime_Hours_Unplanned.sum()}), include_groups=False).reset_index()
pma['mi']=pma.Month.map({m:i for i,m in enumerate(order)}); pma=pma.sort_values(['Plant_Name','mi'])

plant_slopes = {}
for p,d in pma.groupby('Plant_Name'):

pc['mi']=pc.Month.map({m:i for i,m in enumerate(order)})

    combo_rows.append(dict(Plant=p,Line=pl,

        att_jan=d.attain.iloc[0],att_jun=d.attain.iloc[-1],att_slope=sl('attain'),att_adv=att_adv,
        nflags=sum(fl),watch=int(sum(fl)>=2)))

# ================= COPQ =================

gg['total_copq']=gg[['scrap_c','rework_c','ret_c','compl_c','dt_c']].sum(axis=1)
gg['prod_cost']=gg.mat+gg.labor+gg.maint
gg['copq_pct']=gg.total_copq/gg.prod_cost*100
tot = gg[['scrap','rework','returns','scrap_c','rework_c','ret_c','compl_c','dt_c','total_copq','prod_cost','mat','labor','maint','dt_unp','act_h','labor']].sum()

summary = {
 'scrap_c':tot.scrap*tot_mat_unit,'rework_c':tot.rework*0.4*tot_lab_unit,'ret_c':tot.returns*tot_mat_unit,

j=comp.groupby(['Plant_Name','mkey']).agg(Complaints=('Complaint_ID','count'),Avg_Severity=('sev','mean'),
    Severity_Load=('sev','sum')).reset_index()

mrg['rate']=mrg.n/mrg.units*1000

print("all equipment cap:",eq.Replacement_Cost_USD.sum())
# corr equipment age vs downtime
print("corr age~avg monthly dt:",round(eq.age.corr(eq.Avg_Monthly_Downtime_Hours),3),"| cond~dt:",round(eq.Condition_Rating_1to10.corr(eq.Avg_Monthly_Downtime_Hours),3))

# employees
emp=pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Employee_Headcount')

print("\n",eh.round(2).to_string())

# COPQ numbers preview

   rework=('Units_Reworked','sum'),returns=('Customer_Returns','sum'),mat=('Raw_Material_Cost_USD','sum'),
   labor=('Labor_Cost_USD','sum'),maint=('Maintenance_Cost_USD','sum'),dt_unp=('Downtime_Hours_Unplanned','sum'),

gg['mat_unit']=gg.mat/gg.units; gg['lab_unit']=gg.labor/gg.units; gg['hr_rate']=gg.labor/gg.act_h
cs=comp.groupby('Plant_Name').Severity.value_counts().unstack(fill_value=0)
cs=cs.reindex(columns=['Critical','High','Medium','Low'],fill_value=0)
W={'Critical':5000,'High':2500,'Medium':1000,'Low':250}
gg['scrap_c']=gg.scrap*gg.mat_unit; gg['rework_c']=gg.rework*0.4*gg.lab_unit; gg['ret_c']=gg.returns*gg.mat_unit

gg['total']=gg[['scrap_c','rework_c','ret_c','compl_c','dt_c']].sum(axis=1)

[{"content": "MERIDIAN ADVANCED MANUFACTURING INC.
Precision Engineering  |  Aerospace  |  Automotive  |  Industrial Equipment
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
1.  BACKGROUND
Meridian Advanced Manufacturing Inc. is a mid-market precision manufacturing company operating four production facilities across the United States. Since our founding, we have built a reputation for delivering high-tolerance, precision-engineered components to clients in the aerospace, automotive, and industrial equipment sectors. Our total revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $187 million, supported by a workforce of approximately 820 employees across all plants.
Our manufacturing footprint is as follows:
The Columbus plant is our oldest and largest facility, serving as the primary production hub for our aerospace clients. Portland and Nashville were established to expand capacity and diversify our manufacturing capabilities into adjacent markets. The Phoenix plant represents our strategic investment in next-generation manufacturing technologies, including additive manufacturing and advanced composite materials.
2.  CURRENT SITUATION
The Board of Directors has expressed significant concern regarding several converging operational challenges that are eroding our competitive position and financial performance. I am requesting this assessment because the data from the first half of 2024 suggests these issues are systemic and require a structured, analytically rigorous response.
The primary areas of concern are:
Declining Operating Margins: Our consolidated operating margin declined from 14.2% in FY2022 to 11.8% in FY2023, representing a 240-basis-point compression. Preliminary Q1/Q2 2024 figures suggest this trend is continuing, with operating margin tracking at approximately 10.9%. If unaddressed, this trajectory will jeopardize our ability to fund planned capital investments and maintain competitive pricing.
Quality Escalations: Several of our key accounts—including two Tier 1 aerospace OEMs—have formally escalated quality complaints over the past two quarters. Our internal quality metrics show an increase in defect rates, particularly at the Columbus and Portland plants. INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
1.  BACKGROUND
Meridian Advanced Manufacturing Inc. is a mid-market precision manufacturing company operating four production facilities across the United States. Since our founding, we have built a reputation for delivering high-tolerance, precision-engineered components to clients in the aerospace, automotive, and industrial equipment sectors. Our total revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $187 million, supported by a workforce of approximately 820 employees across all plants.
Our manufacturing footprint is as follows:
The Columbus plant is our oldest and largest facility, serving as the primary production hub for our aerospace clients. Portland and Nashville were established to expand capacity and diversify our manufacturing capabilities into adjacent markets. The Phoenix plant represents our strategic investment in next-generation manufacturing technologies, including additive manufacturing and advanced composite materials.
2.  CURRENT SITUATION
The Board of Directors has expressed significant concern regarding several converging operational challenges that are eroding our competitive position and financial performance. I am requesting this assessment because the data from the first half of 2024 suggests these issues are systemic and require a structured, analytically rigorous response.
The primary areas of concern are:
Declining Operating Margins: Our consolidated operating margin declined from 14.2% in FY2022 to 11.8% in FY2023, representing a 240-basis-point compression. Preliminary Q1/Q2 2024 figures suggest this trend is continuing, with operating margin tracking at approximately 10.9%. If unaddressed, this trajectory will jeopardize our ability to fund planned capital investments and maintain competitive pricing.
Quality Escalations: Several of our key accounts—including two Tier 1 aerospace OEMs—have formally escalated quality complaints over the past two quarters. Our internal quality metrics show an increase in defect rates, particularly at the Columbus and Portland plants. Customer satisfaction scores have declined from 4.3/5.0 in FY2022 to 3.7/5.0 in the most recent survey period.
Portland Delivery Performance: The Portland plant has experienced a marked decline in on-time delivery performance over the past two quarters, falling from 94.1% in Q3/Q4 2023 to an estimated 87.3% in Q1/Q2 2024. This is below our contractual SLA threshold of 92% for several accounts and poses a material risk to client retention.
Columbus Equipment & Maintenance: The Columbus facility, our oldest plant, is experiencing escalating unplanned maintenance events. Equipment downtime has increased roughly 18% year-over-year, and maintenance expenditures now represent a disproportionate share of the plant's operating costs. Several critical CNC machines are approaching end-of-life and require either major overhaul or replacement.
Phoenix Ramp-Up Delays: Despite being operational for over two years, the Phoenix facility has not yet achieved its targeted capacity utilization rate of 72%. Current utilization is estimated at approximately 58%, resulting in higher-than-projected per-unit costs and an extended timeline to achieve return on the initial capital investment.
3.  SCOPE OF WORK
I am engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive operational efficiency assessment covering the first two quarters of fiscal year 2024. The assessment should be data-driven, benchmarked against recognized industry standards, and grounded in established operational excellence methodologies. Specifically, I am asking the management analyst team to undertake the following:
Operational Data Analysis: Analyze the attached Q1/Q2 2024 operational data across all four manufacturing plants. This includes production volumes, capacity utilization, defect rates, on-time delivery metrics, labor productivity, equipment downtime, and cost breakdowns. Identify statistically significant trends, anomalies, and cross-plant performance disparities.
Industry Benchmarking: Benchmark Meridian's operational performance against relevant industry standards. Utilize the provided FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) manufacturing capacity utilization data and the manufacturing defect benchmarking dataset to contextualize our performance within the broader U.S. manufacturing sector. Identify areas where we are significantly above or below industry norms.
Bottleneck Identification: Identify the top 3–5 operational bottlenecks or systemic problem areas across the organization. For each identified issue, provide supporting data, assess the financial impact, and determine whether the root cause is related to equipment, process, workforce, or management factors.
Lean Manufacturing Best Practices: Reference established lean manufacturing principles and the EPA lean manufacturing case studies provided for reference. Assess the applicability of specific lean tools and methodologies (e.g., value stream mapping, 5S, TPM, kaizen) to Meridian's identified problem areas. Provide actionable recommendations grounded in proven industry practices.
Excel Workbook — Data Analysis & Findings: Organize all analytical findings, data summaries, benchmarking comparisons, and supporting calculations into a structured Excel workbook. The workbook should be clearly organized with separate worksheets for each major analysis area, include data visualizations where appropriate, and serve as the analytical foundation for the executive presentation.
Executive PowerPoint Presentation: Prepare a professional PowerPoint presentation of approximately 15–20 slides for the executive leadership team. The presentation should cover: (a) current state assessment with key performance metrics, (b) industry benchmarking analysis, (c) identified operational problems with root cause analysis, (d) prioritized recommendations with estimated financial impact and implementation timeline, and (e) a proposed roadmap for operational improvement initiatives.
4.  KEY QUESTIONS TO ADDRESS
The following questions should serve as a guiding framework for the analysis. The executive committee will expect clear, evidence-based answers to each of these in the final presentation:
Which plant(s) require the most urgent operational intervention, and what specific evidence supports this prioritization?
What are the primary drivers of the declining consolidated operating margin? To what extent are these driven by cost inflation, operational inefficiency, pricing pressure, or product mix changes?
How does Meridian's capacity utilization across each plant compare to the national manufacturing average as reported by the Federal Reserve? Where are the largest gaps?
What specific lean manufacturing practices and methodologies could be adopted or expanded to measurably improve operational performance at each facility?
What is the estimated return on investment (ROI) for the top recommended improvement initiatives, including projected timeline to realization and required capital or operational investment?
5.  TIMELINE & DELIVERABLES
Given the urgency of the board's concerns, I am establishing the following timeline for this engagement:
The final presentation will be delivered to the Executive Committee on August 22, 2024. I will be present to provide operational context and support the discussion. Please plan for a 45-minute presentation followed by a 30-minute Q&A session.
6.  ATTACHMENTS & REFERENCE MATERIALS
The following data files and reference documents are provided to support your analysis. Please review all materials thoroughly before the project kickoff meeting:

■  FRED_industrial_production_manufacturing.csv — FRED industrial production index for the manufacturing sector, providing macroeconomic context for Meridian's production volume trends.
■  manufacturing_defect_dataset.csv — Industry benchmarking dataset containing defect rate data across various manufacturing sub-sectors, to be used for comparative quality analysis.
■  EPA_Lean_Manufacturing_Case_Studies.pdf — U.S. Environmental Protection Agency compilation of lean manufacturing case studies demonstrating proven efficiency improvement methodologies applicable to precision manufacturing operations.
This assessment is a high priority for both my office and the Board of Directors. I expect a thorough, analytically rigorous review that will provide the executive committee with clear visibility into our operational challenges and a credible path forward. Please do not hesitate to reach out to me or my Chief of Staff, Sarah Martinez (s.martinez@meridianmfg.com), if you require additional data, access to plant personnel, or clarification on any aspect of this engagement.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
prod = pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Monthly_Production_Data')
comp = pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/Meridian_Customer_Complaints_Q1Q2_2024.csv')
eq   = pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Equipment_Inventory')
bench= pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/manufacturing_defect_dataset.csv')
order=['Jan-2024','Feb-2024','Mar-2024','Apr-2024','May-2024','Jun-2024']

g = prod.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(units=('Production_Volume_Units','sum'),target=('Production_Target_Units','sum'),
    act_h=('Actual_Output_Hours','sum'),plan_h=('Planned_Output_Hours','sum'),defects=('Defect_Count','sum'),
    rework=('Units_Reworked','sum'),scrap=('Scrap_Units','sum'),mat=('Raw_Material_Cost_USD','sum'),
    labor=('Labor_Cost_USD','sum'),maint=('Maintenance_Cost_USD','sum'),dt_unp=('Downtime_Hours_Unplanned','sum'),
    dt_plan=('Downtime_Hours_Planned','sum'),returns=('Customer_Returns','sum'))
g['otd']=prod.groupby('Plant_Name').apply(lambda d: np.average(d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct,weights=d.Production_Volume_Units),include_groups=False)

# ---- watch items per combo ----
pc=prod.copy(); pc['def1000']=pc.Defect_Count/pc.Production_Volume_Units*1000
pc['attain']=pc.Production_Volume_Units/pc.Production_Target_Units*100
pc['mi']=pc.Month.map({m:i for i,m in enumerate(order)})
rows=[]
for (p,pl),d in pc.groupby(['Plant_Name','Product_Line']):
    d=d.sort_values('mi')
    defs=np.diff(d.def1000.values); otds=np.diff(d.otd if False else d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct.values); atts=np.diff(d.attain.values)
    def_adv=int((defs>0).sum()); otd_adv=int((otds<0).sum()); att_adv=int((atts<0).sum())
    sl=lambda c: np.polyfit(d.mi,d[c],1)[0]
    flags=def_adv>=3,otd_adv>=3,att_adv>=3
    rows.append(dict(Plant=p,Line=pl,def1000_start=d.def1000.iloc[0],def1000_end=d.def1000.iloc[-1],
        otd_start=d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct.iloc[0],otd_end=d.On_Time_Delivery_Pct.iloc[-1],
        att_start=d.attain.iloc[0],att_end=d.attain.iloc[-1],
        def_adv_mos=def_adv,otd_adv_mos=otd_adv,att_adv_mos=att_adv,
        def_slope=sl('def1000'),otd_slope=sl('On_Time_Delivery_Pct'),att_slope=sl('attain'),
        n_flag=sum(flags),watch=int(sum(flags)>=2)))
w=pd.DataFrame(rows); print(w.round(2).to_string())
print("\nWATCH ITEMS:", w[w.watch==1][['Plant','Line']].values.tolist())

# ---- FRED ----
fred=pd.read_csv('/work/task_folder/references/FRED_manufacturing_capacity_utilization.csv',parse_dates=['observation_date'])
f24=fred[(fred.observation_date>='2024-01-01')&(fred.observation_date<='2024-06-01')]
print("\nFRED Jan-Jun24 avg:",round(f24.MCUMFN.mean(),2))

# ---- benchmark percentiles ----
d25,d50,d75=np.percentile(bench.DefectRate,[25,50,75]); t25,t50,t75=np.percentile(bench.DowntimePercentage,[25,50,75])
print("DefectRate pct 25/50/75:",round(d25,3),round(d50,3),round(d75,3),"| Downtime pct:",round(t25,3),round(t50,3),round(t75,3))
mer_def=(g.defects/g.units*100); mer_dt=(g.dt_unp/g.plan_h*100)
print("Meridian defect%:",mer_def.round(2).to_dict())
print("Meridian downtime% (unp/planned):",mer_dt.round(2).to_dict())
print("Meridian downtime% (unp/(unp+plan)):",(g.dt_unp/(g.dt_unp+g.dt_plan)*100).round(2).to_dict())
print("bench DowntimePercentage min/max:",bench.DowntimePercentage.min().round(3),bench.DowntimePercentage.max().round(3))
for p in g.index:
    dv=mer_def[p]; tv=mer_dt[p]
    dp='<=P25' if dv<=d25 else '<=P50' if dv<=d50 else '<=P75' if dv<=d75 else '>P75'
    tp='<=P25' if tv<=t25 else '<=P50' if tv<=t50 else '<=P75' if tv<=t75 else '>P75'
    print(p,"defect",round(dv,2),dp,"| downtime",round(tv,2),tp)

# ---- complaint crossref ----
comp['mkey']=pd.to_datetime(comp.Date_Received).dt.month
comp['sev']=comp.Severity.map({'Critical':4,'High':3,'Medium':2,'Low':1})
pm2=prod.copy(); pm2['mkey']=pd.to_datetime(pm2.Month,format='%b-%Y').dt.month
j=comp.groupby(['Plant_Name','mkey']).agg(n=('Complaint_ID','count'),sevavg=('sev','mean'),sevsum=('sev','sum')).reset_index()
jj=pm2.groupby(['Plant_Name','mkey']).agg(units=('Production_Volume_Units','sum'),dt=('Downtime_Hours_Unplanned','sum')).reset_index()
mrg=j.merge(jj,on=['Plant_Name','mkey'],how='right').fillna({'n':0,'sevavg':0,'sevsum':0})
mrg['rate']=mrg.n/mrg.units*1000
print("\n",mrg.round(2).to_string())
mc=mrg[mrg.n>0]
print("corr complaints~downtime (all 24 pm):",round(mrg.n.corr(mrg.dt),3),"| spearman:",round(mrg.n.corr(mrg.dt,method='spearman'),3))
print("corr severity~downtime (complaint months):",round(mc.sevavg.corr(mc.dt),3),"| spearman:",round(mc.sevavg.corr(mc.dt,method='spearman'),3))
print("corr sevsum~downtime:",round(mrg.sevsum.corr(mrg.dt),3))
for p,d in mrg.groupby('Plant_Name'):
    dd=d[d.n>0]
    print(f"  {p}: n~dt {d.n.corr(d.dt):.3f} | sev~dt {dd.sevavg.corr(dd.dt) if len(dd)>2 else float('nan'):.3f} | complaints {d.n.sum():.0f} rate {d.n.sum()/d.units.sum()*1000:.2f}/1000")

# ---- equipment ----
eq['age']=2024-eq.Year_Installed
eq['yrs_since_ovh']=2024-pd.to_datetime(eq.Last_Major_Overhaul,format='%b-%Y').dt.year
eq['flag']=(eq.age>8)&(eq.Condition_Rating_1to10<=5)
print("\n",eq.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(items=('Equipment_ID','count'),avg_age=('age','mean'),avg_cond=('Condition_Rating_1to10','mean'),
   flags=('flag','sum'),cap=('Replacement_Cost_USD',lambda s: s[eq.loc[s.index,'flag']].sum()),
   avg_dt=('Avg_Monthly_Downtime_Hours','mean')).round(2).to_string())
print(eq[eq.flag][['Plant_Name','Equipment_ID','Equipment_Type','Year_Installed','Last_Major_Overhaul','Condition_Rating_1to10','Avg_Monthly_Downtime_Hours','Replacement_Cost_USD','yrs_since_ovh','age']].to_string())
print("total flag cap:",eq[eq.flag].Replacement_Cost_USD.sum())

# ---- employees & labor productivity ----
emp=pd.read_excel('/work/task_folder/Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx','Employee_Headcount')
eh=emp.groupby('Plant_Name').agg(FT=('Headcount_FT','sum'),PT=('Headcount_PT','sum'),tenure=('Avg_Tenure_Years','mean'),turnover=('Turnover_Rate_Pct_Annual','mean'),training=('Avg_Training_Hours_Per_Employee','mean'))
eh['total']=eh.FT+eh.PT
u=prod.groupby('Plant_Name').Production_Volume_Units.sum()
eh['units_per_emp']=u/eh.total
eh['labor_per_unit']=g.labor/u
print("\n",eh.round(2).to_string())
print("Phoenix production dept:", emp[(emp.Plant_Name=='Phoenix AZ')].to_string())
EOF", "description": "Finish trend, benchmark, complaint, equipment analyses"}

Precision Engineering  |  Aerospace  |  Automotive  |  Industrial Equipment
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
1.  BACKGROUND
Meridian Advanced Manufacturing Inc. is a mid-market precision manufacturing company operating four production facilities across the United States. Since our founding, we have built a reputation for delivering high-tolerance, precision-engineered components to clients in the aerospace, automotive, and industrial equipment sectors. Our total revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $187 million, supported by a workforce of approximately 820 employees across all plants.
Our manufacturing footprint is as follows:
The Columbus plant is our oldest and largest facility, serving as the primary production hub for our aerospace clients. Portland and Nashville were established to expand capacity and diversify our manufacturing capabilities into adjacent markets. The Phoenix plant represents our strategic investment in next-generation manufacturing technologies, including additive manufacturing and advanced composite materials.
2.  CURRENT SITUATION
The Board of Directors has expressed significant concern regarding several converging operational challenges that are eroding our competitive position and financial performance. I am requesting this assessment because the data from the first half of 2024 suggests these issues are systemic and require a structured, analytically rigorous response.
The primary areas of concern are:
Declining Operating Margins: Our consolidated operating margin declined from 14.2% in FY2022 to 11.8% in FY2023, representing a 240-basis-point compression. Preliminary Q1/Q2 2024 figures suggest this trend is continuing, with operating margin tracking at approximately 10.9%. If unaddressed, this trajectory will jeopardize our ability to fund planned capital investments and maintain competitive pricing.
Quality Escalations: Several of our key accounts—including two Tier 1 aerospace OEMs—have formally escalated quality complaints over the past two quarters. Our internal quality metrics show an increase in defect rates, particularly at the Columbus and Portland plants. Customer satisfaction scores have declined from 4.3/5.0 in FY2022 to 3.7/5.0 in the most recent survey period.
Portland Delivery Performance: The Portland plant has experienced a marked decline in on-time delivery performance over the past two quarters, falling from 94.1% in Q3/Q4 2023 to an estimated 87.3% in Q1/Q2 2024. This is below our contractual SLA threshold of 92% for several accounts and poses a material risk to client retention.
Columbus Equipment & Maintenance: The Columbus facility, our oldest plant, is experiencing escalating unplanned maintenance events. Equipment downtime has increased roughly 18% year-over-year, and maintenance expenditures now represent a disproportionate share of the plant's operating costs. Several critical CNC machines are approaching end-of-life and require either major overhaul or replacement.
Phoenix Ramp-Up Delays: Despite being operational for over two years, the Phoenix facility has not yet achieved its targeted capacity utilization rate of 72%. Current utilization is estimated at approximately 58%, resulting in higher-than-projected per-unit costs and an extended timeline to achieve return on the initial capital investment.
3.  SCOPE OF WORK
I am engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive operational efficiency assessment covering the first two quarters of fiscal year 2024. The assessment should be data-driven, benchmarked against recognized industry standards, and grounded in established operational excellence methodologies. Specifically, I am asking the management analyst team to undertake the following:
Operational Data Analysis: Analyze the attached Q1/Q2 2024 operational data across all four manufacturing plants. This includes production volumes, capacity utilization, defect rates, on-time delivery metrics, labor productivity, equipment downtime, and cost breakdowns. Identify statistically significant trends, anomalies, and cross-plant performance disparities.
Industry Benchmarking: Benchmark Meridian's operational performance against relevant industry standards. Utilize the provided FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) manufacturing capacity utilization data and the manufacturing defect benchmarking dataset to contextualize our performance within the broader U.S. manufacturing sector. Identify areas where we are significantly above or below industry norms.
Bottleneck Identification: Identify the top 3–5 operational bottlenecks or systemic problem areas across the organization. For each identified issue, provide supporting data, assess the financial impact, and determine whether the root cause is related to equipment, process, workforce, or management factors.
Lean Manufacturing Best Practices: Reference established lean manufacturing principles and the EPA lean manufacturing case studies provided for reference. Assess the applicability of specific lean tools and methodologies (e.g., value stream mapping, 5S, TPM, kaizen) to Meridian's identified problem areas. Provide actionable recommendations grounded in proven industry practices.
Excel Workbook — Data Analysis & Findings: Organize all analytical findings, data summaries, benchmarking comparisons, and supporting calculations into a structured Excel workbook. The workbook should be clearly organized with separate worksheets for each major analysis area, include data visualizations where appropriate, and serve as the analytical foundation for the executive presentation.
Executive PowerPoint Presentation: Prepare a professional PowerPoint presentation of approximately 15–20 slides for the executive leadership team. The presentation should cover: (a) current state assessment with key performance metrics, (b) industry benchmarking analysis, (c) identified operational problems with root cause analysis, (d) prioritized recommendations with estimated financial impact and implementation timeline, and (e) a proposed roadmap for operational improvement initiatives.
4.  KEY QUESTIONS TO ADDRESS
The following questions should serve as a guiding framework for the analysis. The executive committee will expect clear, evidence-based answers to each of these in the final presentation:
Which plant(s) require the most urgent operational intervention, and what specific evidence supports this prioritization?
What are the primary drivers of the declining consolidated operating margin? To what extent are these driven by cost inflation, operational inefficiency, pricing pressure, or product mix changes?
How does Meridian's capacity utilization across each plant compare to the national manufacturing average as reported by the Federal Reserve? Where are the largest gaps?
What specific lean manufacturing practices and methodologies could be adopted or expanded to measurably improve operational performance at each facility?
What is the estimated return on investment (ROI) for the top recommended improvement initiatives, including projected timeline to realization and required capital or operational investment?
5.  TIMELINE & DELIVERABLES
Given the urgency of the board's concerns, I am establishing the following timeline for this engagement:
The final presentation will be delivered to the Executive Committee on August 22, 2024. I will be present to provide operational context and support the discussion. Please plan for a 45-minute presentation followed by a 30-minute Q&A session.
6.  ATTACHMENTS & REFERENCE MATERIALS
The following data files and reference documents are provided to support your analysis. Please review all materials thoroughly before the project kickoff meeting:
■  Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx — Detailed operational data for all four plants covering January–June 2024, including monthly production volumes, capacity utilization rates, defect counts, on-time delivery rates, labor hours, equipment downtime logs, and cost allocations.
■  Meridian_Customer_Complaints_Q1Q2_2024.csv — Log of all customer complaints and quality escalations received during Q1/Q2 2024, including complaint category, severity, affected plant, product line, and resolution status.
■  FRED_manufacturing_capacity_utilization.csv — Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) time series for U.S. manufacturing sector capacity utilization, to be used as the primary benchmarking reference for capacity analysis.
■  FRED_industrial_production_manufacturing.csv — FRED industrial production index for the manufacturing sector, providing macroeconomic context for Meridian's production volume trends.
■  manufacturing_defect_dataset.csv — Industry benchmarking dataset containing defect rate data across various manufacturing sub-sectors, to be used for comparative quality analysis.
■  EPA_Lean_Manufacturing_Case_Studies.pdf — U.S. Environmental Protection Agency compilation of lean manufacturing case studies demonstrating proven efficiency improvement methodologies applicable to precision manufacturing operations.
This assessment is a high priority for both my office and the Board of Directors. I expect a thorough, analytically rigorous review that will provide the executive committee with clear visibility into our operational challenges and a credible path forward. Please do not hesitate to reach out to me or my Chief of Staff, Sarah Martinez (s.martinez@meridianmfg.com), if you require additional data, access to plant personnel, or clarification on any aspect of this engagement.
I look forward to your findings and recommendations.
Regards,
David Chen

1.  BACKGROUND
Meridian Advanced Manufacturing Inc. is a mid-market precision manufacturing company operating four production facilities across the United States. Since our founding, we have built a reputation for delivering high-tolerance, precision-engineered components to clients in the aerospace, automotive, and industrial equipment sectors. Our total revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $187 million, supported by a workforce of approximately 820 employees across all plants.
Our manufacturing footprint is as follows:
The Columbus plant is our oldest and largest facility, serving as the primary production hub for our aerospace clients. Portland and Nashville were established to expand capacity and diversify our manufacturing capabilities into adjacent markets. The Phoenix plant represents our strategic investment in next-generation manufacturing technologies, including additive manufacturing and advanced composite materials.
2.  CURRENT SITUATION
The Board of Directors has expressed significant concern regarding several converging operational challenges that are eroding our competitive position and financial performance. I am requesting this assessment because the data from the first half of 2024 suggests these issues are systemic and require a structured, analytically rigorous response.
The primary areas of concern are:
Declining Operating Margins: Our consolidated operating margin declined from 14.2% in FY2022 to 11.8% in FY2023, representing a 240-basis-point compression. Preliminary Q1/Q2 2024 figures suggest this trend is continuing, with operating margin tracking at approximately 10.9%. If unaddressed, this trajectory will jeopardize our ability to fund planned capital investments and maintain competitive pricing.
Quality Escalations: Several of our key accounts—including two Tier 1 aerospace OEMs—have formally escalated quality complaints over the past two quarters. Our internal quality metrics show an increase in defect rates, particularly at the Columbus and Portland plants. Customer satisfaction scores have declined from 4.3/5.0 in FY2022 to 3.7/5.0 in the most recent survey period.
Portland Delivery Performance: The Portland plant has experienced a marked decline in on-time delivery performance over the past two quarters, falling from 94.1% in Q3/Q4 2023 to an estimated 87.3% in Q1/Q2 2024. This is below our contractual SLA threshold of 92% for several accounts and poses a material risk to client retention.
Columbus Equipment & Maintenance: The Columbus facility, our oldest plant, is experiencing escalating unplanned maintenance events. Equipment downtime has increased roughly 18% year-over-year, and maintenance expenditures now represent a disproportionate share of the plant's operating costs. Several critical CNC machines are approaching end-of-life and require either major overhaul or replacement.
Phoenix Ramp-Up Delays: Despite being operational for over two years, the Phoenix facility has not yet achieved its targeted capacity utilization rate of 72%. Current utilization is estimated at approximately 58%, resulting in higher-than-projected per-unit costs and an extended timeline to achieve return on the initial capital investment.
3.  SCOPE OF WORK
I am engaging your team to conduct a comprehensive operational efficiency assessment covering the first two quarters of fiscal year 2024. The assessment should be data-driven, benchmarked against recognized industry standards, and grounded in established operational excellence methodologies. Specifically, I am asking the management analyst team to undertake the following:
Operational Data Analysis: Analyze the attached Q1/Q2 2024 operational data across all four manufacturing plants. This includes production volumes, capacity utilization, defect rates, on-time delivery metrics, labor productivity, equipment downtime, and cost breakdowns. Identify statistically significant trends, anomalies, and cross-plant performance disparities.
Industry Benchmarking: Benchmark Meridian's operational performance against relevant industry standards. Utilize the provided FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) manufacturing capacity utilization data and the manufacturing defect benchmarking dataset to contextualize our performance within the broader U.S. manufacturing sector. Identify areas where we are significantly above or below industry norms.
Bottleneck Identification: Identify the top 3–5 operational bottlenecks or systemic problem areas across the organization. For each identified issue, provide supporting data, assess the financial impact, and determine whether the root cause is related to equipment, process, workforce, or management factors.
Lean Manufacturing Best Practices: Reference established lean manufacturing principles and the EPA lean manufacturing case studies provided for reference. Assess the applicability of specific lean tools and methodologies (e.g., value stream mapping, 5S, TPM, kaizen) to Meridian's identified problem areas. Provide actionable recommendations grounded in proven industry practices.
Excel Workbook — Data Analysis & Findings: Organize all analytical findings, data summaries, benchmarking comparisons, and supporting calculations into a structured Excel workbook. The workbook should be clearly organized with separate worksheets for each major analysis area, include data visualizations where appropriate, and serve as the analytical foundation for the executive presentation.
Executive PowerPoint Presentation: Prepare a professional PowerPoint presentation of approximately 15–20 slides for the executive leadership team. The presentation should cover: (a) current state assessment with key performance metrics, (b) industry benchmarking analysis, (c) identified operational problems with root cause analysis, (d) prioritized recommendations with estimated financial impact and implementation timeline, and (e) a proposed roadmap for operational improvement initiatives.
4.  KEY QUESTIONS TO ADDRESS
The following questions should serve as a guiding framework for the analysis. The executive committee will expect clear, evidence-based answers to each of these in the final presentation:
Which plant(s) require the most urgent operational intervention, and what specific evidence supports this prioritization?
What are the primary drivers of the declining consolidated operating margin? To what extent are these driven by cost inflation, operational inefficiency, pricing pressure, or product mix changes?
How does Meridian's capacity utilization across each plant compare to the national manufacturing average as reported by the Federal Reserve? Where are the largest gaps?
What specific lean manufacturing practices and methodologies could be adopted or expanded to measurably improve operational performance at each facility?
What is the estimated return on investment (ROI) for the top recommended improvement initiatives, including projected timeline to realization and required capital or operational investment?
5.  TIMELINE & DELIVERABLES
Given the urgency of the board's concerns, I am establishing the following timeline for this engagement:
The final presentation will be delivered to the Executive Committee on August 22, 2024. I will be present to provide operational context and support the discussion. Please plan for a 45-minute presentation followed by a 30-minute Q&A session.
6.  ATTACHMENTS & REFERENCE MATERIALS
The following data files and reference documents are provided to support your analysis. Please review all materials thoroughly before the project kickoff meeting:
■  Meridian_Plant_Operations_Q1Q2_2024.xlsx — Detailed operational data for all four plants covering January–June 2024, including monthly production volumes, capacity utilization rates, defect counts, on-time delivery rates, labor hours, equipment downtime logs, and cost allocations.
■  Meridian_Customer_Complaints_Q1Q2_2024.csv — Log of all customer complaints and quality escalations received during Q1/Q2 2024, including complaint category, severity, affected plant, product line, and resolution status.
■  FRED_manufacturing_capacity_utilization.csv — Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) time series for U.S. manufacturing sector capacity utilization, to be used as the primary benchmarking reference for capacity analysis.
■  FRED_industrial_production_manufacturing.csv — FRED industrial production index for the manufacturing sector, providing macroeconomic context for Meridian's production volume trends.
■  manufacturing_defect_dataset.csv — Industry benchmarking dataset containing defect rate data across various manufacturing sub-sectors, to be used for comparative quality analysis.
■  EPA_Lean_Manufacturing_Case_Studies.pdf — U.S. Environmental Protection Agency compilation of lean manufacturing case studies demonstrating proven efficiency improvement methodologies applicable to precision manufacturing operations.
This assessment is a high priority for both my office and the Board of Directors. I expect a thorough, analytically rigorous review that will provide the executive committee with clear visibility into our operational challenges and a credible path forward. Please do not hesitate to reach out to me or my Chief of Staff, Sarah Martinez (s.martinez@meridianmfg.com), if you require additional data, access to plant personnel, or clarification on any aspect of this engagement.
I look forward to your findings and recommendations.
